title: Meet the Team
intro: Retro Porting Toolkit is a collaborative project. The people below build the recompilers, the runtimes, the tooling around them, and this site. Not every project mentioned across the site is owned or maintained by the same person, so each entry says what that person actually works on.

members.name: Matthew Stanley
members.role: Team lead, ecosystem developer and maintainer
bio: Without AI, reverse engineered a shutdown live service hero shooter for PC to bring the game back from the dead.
Backend web services and data engineer with over ten years of experience.

Applied those skills, together with a background in classic games and decompilation and recompilation, to build out the NES, Super Nintendo, Game Boy Advance, Nintendo DS, Virtual Boy and PlayStation recompilers.

members.name: Jack Rickey
bio: Quantitative developer and systems programmer: builds the full stack behind trading decisions by day, and writes open source low-level systems tooling by night.
BattleShip is a cross-platform native PC port of Super Smash Bros. for the Nintendo 64, decompiled and ported with AI assistance.

members.name: Alex Vanderveen
members.role: Primary developer, RetComM Launcher, recomp-net and retcomm-rbengine
bio: The RetComM Launcher is a single front end for updating, managing and distributing static recompilations.
recomp-net and retcomm-rbengine bring netplay, save states and rewinding to several recompilation platforms.
A significant contributor to PSXRecomp and SNESRecomp.

members.name: Alexandros Mandravillis
bio: Cloud security engineer, SRE and network security architect by day.
A significant contributor to PSXRecomp, working in breadth: dozens of recompiled titles, and dozens of pull requests to the PSXRecomp infrastructure itself.

members.name: Shokunin
members.role: UI/UX, frontend and marketing, across the website and the launchers
bio: Product and R&D builder with two decades of experience across 50+ games and emerging technology.

Explores how AI-assisted development can expand what small teams can build around classic games, and leads the interface, frontend and marketing work behind the Retro Porting Toolkit website and launchers.
